name: Cheese (food medium)
description: Food-derived medium: metabolizable components of Cheese [Milk and milk products] from FooDB, plus a standard M9 mineral base. Organic components use presence-based uptake bounds; FooDB content retained. Measured compounds with no BiGG exchange are listed under uncovered.

provenance.citation: FooDB v2020-04-07 (Wishart DS et al., foodb.ca). Content sources: DTU, USDA.
provenance.notes: Organic components mapped from FooDB compounds to BiGG via InChIKey/name. Mineral base added. Bounds presence-based; foodb_content retained. Unmapped measured compounds kept in uncovered (v2 completeness fix). IMPORTANT: composition values are taken from the archived FooDB 2020-04-07 CSV data release; FooDB's live food page no longer displays this bulk composition, so it will appear empty. Verify individual compounds via the per-component cross-reference links. Underlying content was aggregated by FooDB from USDA / DTU / Phenol Explorer.
provenance.verification: expert-curated (multi-source food composition; growth-relevant profile completed, FooDB noise removed)
curation_sources: USDA FDC 328637 (Cheese, cheddar) — macronutrients, fatty acids, minerals, most vitamins
USDA FDC 173414 (SR Legacy, Cheese, cheddar) — full amino-acid profile, choline, vitamin D, beta-carotene, C15:0
USDA FDC 171292 (Cheese, cheddar reduced fat) — vitamin D / choline cross-check
Zhang et al. 2023, Food Science & Nutrition, PMC10171539 — HPLC carbohydrates + organic acids across cheddar/parmesan/mozzarella/swiss
Marsili et al. HPLC organic acids in cheese/milk/whey (J Food Sci) — lactic/citric/acetic/formic cross-check
FooDB FOOD00617 (Cheese) — component inventory being curated
UK McCance & Widdowson CoFID / EFSA + FRIDA — dairy iodine and biotin
provenance.curation_notes: Dominant carbon/energy source for a microbe growing on cheese is LACTIC ACID (~1.4 g/100g), not sugar: lactose is almost fully fermented during ripening, leaving only residual lactose (~0.1 g) and free galactose (~0.27 g). After lactate, the growth substrates are the free-amino-acid/peptide pool from casein proteolysis (glutamate, proline, leucine highest) and milk-fat free fatty acids from lipolysis. Composition modeled on aged cheddar-type cheese as the generic 'Cheese' reference; organic-acid
curation_added: lactic acid (dominant organic acid / main fermentable carbon source)
D-galactose and residual lactose with real amounts (replacing sucrose/maltose/starch)
palmitic acid C16:0 (largest single fatty acid)
vitamin K2 (MK-4) split from total K

curation_removed.name: Starch C12H20O10
curation_removed.reason: cheese contains no starch; implausible for a dairy matrix (FooDB artifact)

curation_removed.name: Sucrose C12H22O11
curation_removed.reason: not present in cheese; milk sugar is lactose only, and it is fermented away (FooDB artifact)

curation_removed.name: Maltose C12H22O11
curation_removed.reason: not present in cheese; no starch hydrolysis source (FooDB artifact)

curation_removed.name: L-Ascorbate
curation_removed.reason: vitamin C is ~0 mg/100g in cheese; not a real nutrient of this food (FooDB artifact)

curation_removed.name: Eicosapentaenoic acid
curation_removed.reason: EPA (C20:5 n-3) is a marine fatty acid present only at negligible trace in ruminant milk fat; not a defining or growth-relevant nutrient of cheese

curation_removed.name: Doconexent
curation_removed.reason: DHA (C22:6 n-3) is a marine fatty acid, negligible trace in milk fat; not growth-relevant (FooDB over-listing)

curation_removed.name: Alpha-Carotene
curation_removed.reason: only trace in milk fat; effectively negligible vs beta-carotene which is kept (predicted/over-listed)

curation_removed.name: Beta-Cryptoxanthin
curation_removed.reason: negligible trace carotenoid in cheese; not growth-relevant (over-listed)

curation_removed.name: Gadoleic acid
curation_removed.reason: C20:1 present only at trace in milk fat; not growth-relevant

curation_removed.name: Gamolenic acid
curation_removed.reason: GLA (C18:3 n-6) negligible trace in milk fat; not a defining nutrient

basis: per 100 g fresh weight; representative aged/hard cheese (cheddar-type) used as the reference matrix for generic 'Cheese'

coverage_source.definition: pct_covered_all = components / (components + unresolved ingredients) — the legacy metric, which counts pipeline-derived components as covered. pct_covered_source = source-stated components / (those + unresolved ingredients + ingredients replaced by derived components). Component classes come from tools/component_evidence_classes.tsv. A null value means the denominator was zero; it does not mean 100.
